items.title: Larry — ИИ-агент на старом игровом ПК, который продвигает приложения в TikTok (Oliver Henry)
items.summary_ru: Oliver Henry (не студент — разработчик, сотрудник RevenueCat) поставил на старый игровой ПК Ubuntu и агент OpenClaw на модели Claude и назвал его Larry. Larry сам делает TikTok-слайдшоу для двух его iOS-приложений (Snugly — редизайн комнаты, Liply — превью губ), пишет подписи и выкладывает черновики через Postiz. По словам автора: 500 000 просмотров меньше чем за неделю, 108 платящих подписчиков и ≈ $588 MRR; позже ≈ $714 MRR (Luminary Lane). Пост стоит ≈ $0,50 API. Громкие «$4000 за неделю» — в основном мем-монета, созданная фанатами, и партнёрские ссылки — это не повторяемая часть.
steps: Ключевая идея: агент отвечает за всю воронку — контент → просмотры → установки → оплаты (RevenueCat) — и сам правит слабое звено.
Нужен свой продукт или партнёрский оффер: агент продвигает, а не создаёт ценность из воздуха.
Поставьте OpenClaw (github.com/openclaw/openclaw) на ПК или отдельную машину с Ubuntu.
Установите навык Larry (github.com/OllieWazza/LarrySkill) — в песочнице: навык хранит много API-ключей.
Подключите Postiz для публикации и аналитику дохода; музыку и финальную публикацию автор добавлял вручную (~60 с на пост).
Считайте не просмотры, а платящих клиентов: «200K просмотров без конверсий ничего не стоят».

items.title: How to continue a Claude Code task in Codex without re-explaining it
items.summary: If you use more than one AI coding agent, you have probably hit this. Claude Code stops at a usage limit halfway through a task. You open Codex to keep going, and it knows nothing: not the task, not what is done, not what you decided, not what is blocking. So you explain everything again from scratch. I ran into this often, so I built pas-agent , a small open-source CLI that carries a task from one agent to the next. This post shows how to use it to move a task from Claude Code to Codex. items.title: We Audited Live MCP Servers & 20 Top SaaS Vendors: OWASP MCP03 Tool Poisoning, 200-Day TLS & AI Subprocessors
items.summary: Enterprise engineering and security teams face two parallel external attack surfaces heading into 2026: MCP tool manifests loaded into AI agents (exposed to hidden prompt injection, credential path harvesting, stealth Unicode smuggling, and schema rug-pulls) and third-party SaaS vendors under EU DORA/NIS2 and tightening Ballot SC-081 (200-day TLS) rules. Developers commit these files to GitHub all the time, usually without anyone reviewing them. So I measured what's in them. The CLI supports a hillclimbing loop:

- run the tasks

-

items.title: I hand-ported dozens of n8n AI templates into standalone agents. Here is what broke.
items.summary: Over the last ten days I have been porting n8n AI templates into single-file JavaScript agents, one at a time, by hand, and offered each one to the template's author. The goal is simple: the author's prompt and logic, unchanged, running as one file on someone else's machine with their own model key. Dozens of ports in, the same handful of problems keep coming up. None of them are about the model. 1. The prompt is the product, so copy it verbatim The temptation is to "clean up" a prompt while you port it. Don't. Authors notice immediately, and the prompt is usually the part they spent the most

Цель проста: авторская подсказка и логика, без изменений, работающие одним файлом на чужой машине со своим ключом модели. Стек: Node.js. Чем полезно: пошаговый разбор, который можно повторить на своём ПК.

items.title: Replit pricing explained: Core, Pro, credits and real hosting bills in 2026
items.summary: Replit costs $20 a month on Core or from $100 a month on Pro, and each plan loads the same amount as monthly credits. Agent work in Free Mode costs nothing within an allowance. Hosting the app, its database and the more capable models all draw on the credits, and usage past them bills as overage. The free Starter plan is closed to new builders, who get a 3-day Core trial instead. For a small app, the plan fee often covers the hosting. The line that grows a bill is the production database, which meters every hour it is active. The prices below come from Replit's pricing page and billing docs as
items.summary_ru: Стоимость Replit составляет 20 долларов в месяц для Core или от 100 долларов в месяц для Pro, и каждый план загружает ту же сумму, что и ежемесячные кредиты. Работа агента в бесплатном режиме не требует никаких затрат в пределах лимита. Хостинг приложения, его базы данных и более мощных моделей требуют кредитов, а использование сверх них оплачивается как перерасход. Зачем вам: готовый инструмент — ставится у себя и встраивается в ваш конвейер.

items.title: Foxit MCP Server: Let Your AI Agent Do the PDF Work.
items.summary: Working with PDFs in code is mostly plumbing. You upload the file, start a job, poll until it's done, download the result, and deal with tokens along the way. Foxit has a guide that shows how to skip most of that by connecting your AI tool to their PDF tools through an MCP server. What it covers Foxit's open-source MCP server, which turns their cloud PDF API into 30+ tools an AI agent can call The tools, in seven groups: making PDFs from Word, Excel, PowerPoint, images, HTML or a web page; turning PDFs back into those formats; merging, splitting, compressing and watermarking; comparing and OCR

Сравнил четыре режима работы: LLM без контекста, с сырыми триплетами из графа, с шаблонами на естественном языке и с фильтрованными шаблонами. Без графа модель показала accuracy 17,37% — она почти всегда отвечала «недостаточно информации». С графовым контекстом accuracy поднялась до 79,21%. Разница между форматами подачи контекста оказалась минимальной. Всё работает полностью локально: без внешних API, на одном ноутбуке. Читать далее

items.summary: I wanted Claude and GitHub Copilot to answer questions from my own notes and documentation, without uploading anything. So I built docs-rag-mcp , an MCP server in C# that indexes a folder of documents and lets any MCP client search it. You point it at a folder of Markdown, text, HTML, Word or PDF files. It splits them into passages, embeds each passage, and stores everything in one SQLite file. When you ask your assistant a question, it calls search_docs and answers from the passages it gets back, with the file and section for each one. claude mcp add docs-rag -- dnx DocsRagMcp --yes With Olla

items.summary: Развернуть n8n просто, а работать с ним — нет. Обновления ломают рабочие сценарии: вчерашний воркфлоу падает, транскрибация из Telegram выдаёт неясную ошибку, модель через российский агрегатор не цепляется. За последний год в n8n нашли пять критических уязвимостей, две из них позволяли выполнять код на сервере без входа в систему. В облачной версии такие дыры латает сам n8n, а на своём сервере следить за патчами и обновляться придётся владельцу или его разработчику. MCP servers started showing up in vulnerability catalogs. Every major agent framework added human approvals, sandboxes or durable runs. uv run python scripts/run_workflow.py 'xs = [i * i for i in range(5)]; print(f"squares: {xs}"); sum(xs)'
uv run durable-mcp-gateway worker   # recovery: prints "durable-mcp-gateway worker ready: ..."

Before an agent pays, it needs an answer to one question: which company is behind this domain, and has anyone proved it? We built Fidem to answer that question for agents. For an ops team the benefit of a Dify/n8n setup is immediate: triaging an alert, summarising an incident, querying runbooks or preparing a post-mortem draft can become visual, self-hosted workflows that you version and monitor. The two tools look alike on screen (nodes linked on a canvas) but they start from different places. Dify is an LLM application development platform: prompts, knowledge bases, agents and workflows are its core objects. n
items.summary_ru: Dify и n8n — это два ответа с открытым исходным кодом на одну и ту же задачу: объединение вызовов LLM, инструментов и существующих систем без необходимости каждый раз писать полное приложение. Для операционной группы преимущества от установки Dify/n8n очевидны: сортировка оповещений, обобщение инцидента, запрос модулей Runbook или подготовка посмертного черновика могут… Зачем вам: готовый инструмент — ставится у себя и встраивается в ваш конвейер.

items.title: Beyond Text Generation: Turning LLMs into Decision Models
items.summary: Let the LLM reason about the problem. Let a decision model choose what happens next. Let deterministic code decide what is allowed to happen. LangChain supplies the basic building blocks (models, prompts, tools, integrations), LangGraph the orchestration. Both projects are among the most-followed on GitHub in the AI agent ecosystem. items.summary: An MCP server is a remote API whose client is a language model. That sentence explains most of the security work. The model is not a trusted caller. It reads text from users, documents, tickets and web pages, and it can be persuaded to pass an argument you did not intend. The protocol gives you discovery and message shapes; it does not give you an authorization model. If the gateway cannot answer who is calling, for which tenant, under which scope, against which tool version, with what budget, and where the trace is , the call should not happen. items.summary: An MCP server is only useful when someone else can install it, authenticate it, and trust what its tools do. That is why "publish to a registry" and "sell it as a product" are two different jobs. A registry helps people find you. A marketplace helps a buyer pay you once the install path and the limits are clear. If you built an MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or another MCP-capable client, you have three distribution paths. Most builders should use more than one. items.title: We measured what memory saves an AI coding agent (and why we won't call it proven yet)

I build OmniMem ( https://omnimem.org/?utm_source=devto&utm_campaign=v7 ), an open source, self-hosted memory server for agents that speak MCP. items.title: Queueing agent runs against a concurrency cap: backpressure, fairness and limit errors
items.summary: The first version of most agent backends starts a sandbox whenever a request arrives. It works until the day twenty users click at once, or one user's agent fans out into fifty parallel tool calls. Then starts begin to fail with limit errors, the agent retries them, and the retries make it worse. Every sandbox platform has a concurrency cap. On Sandscale it is the number of boxes running at once, which the pricing page lists per plan: 3 on Free and 30 on the first paid tiers. items.title: Self-Hosted LLM: How to Host Your Own LLM
items.summary: A self-hosted LLM is worth it in two cases. The first is when your prompts hold data that must not leave servers you control. The second is when you send so many requests that a server running all month costs less than paying per request. On price alone it seldom beats a small hosted model. A cloud server with one 16 GB graphics card costs about US$384 a month at list price before it answers a single question. So the main reason to host your own LLM is where the data goes, not the bill. Второй — когда вы отправляете столько запросов, что работа сервера весь месяц обходится дешевле, чем оплата за каждый запрос. Только по цене он редко превосходит небольшую размещенную модель. items.title: Paperclip: a self-hosted task board where the assignees are AI agents
items.summary: If you use coding agents a lot, you probably know this moment: five terminal tabs, three agents, one half-finished refactor, and no clear record of who was doing what or how much it all cost. On reboot, most of that context is gone. Paperclip is an open-source project aimed at exactly that mess. Its README calls it "open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents". The idea: it looks like a task manager, but the people you assign work to are agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others), and around them sit an org chart, budgets, approvals and goals. items.title: Feeding command output back to an LLM: truncation, cleanup and secret masking
items.summary: An agent runs npm test . The command prints 40,000 lines: progress bars, colour codes, a deprecation warning repeated 900 times, and, at the very end, the one assertion failure that matters. If you pass all of that back as the tool result, you pay for every token, push earlier context out of the window, and make the model hunt for the needle. If you cut it to the first 2,000 characters, the failure is gone. Tool output needs preparing before a model sees it. This post walks through a small TypeScript helper that does four things in order: normalize terminal noise, mask secrets, collapse repeat

make dist           # a dry run of a release, in dist/<version>/ (docs/RELEASING.md)
make companion   # optional: the APK of Pinky on the phone (Android SDK and JDK)
make app         # build/pinky/darwin-<arch>/Pinky.app and pinky-<version>-<arch>.dmg

items.title: Make Claude Code Plan Before It Codes: One Prompt That Kills the "Confident but Wrong" First Draft
items.summary: The most expensive AI coding failure isn't bad code. It's confidently wrong code — a full implementation of the wrong thing, delivered fast, that you now have to review, reject, and re-explain. The fix is boring and it works: make the agent plan first, and make it ask instead of assume. Here is the exact prompt I use, in full: Do not write code yet. Enter plan mode: explore [FEATURE_AREA], then give me a step-by-step plan for [GOAL] with files to change, risks, and tests to run. Flag anything ambiguous as a question instead of assuming. items.title: Git worktrees for parallel AI coding agents: what they fix and what they don't
items.summary: ou want three agents working at once: one on the checkout page, one on a bug, one writing tests. If they share one working copy, they overwrite each other's files mid-task and nobody can tell whose change broke what. The standard answer is git worktrees: one checkout per agent, all backed by the same repository. This guide sets that up, covers the traps people hit in the first hour, and then the part worktrees don't solve: the agents still meet at merge time. One worktree per agent A worktree is a second (third, fourth) checkout of the same repo in its own directory, on its own branch. Commits
items.summary_ru: Вам нужно, чтобы три агента работали одновременно: один на странице оформления заказа, один над ошибкой, один над написанием тестов. Если они используют одну рабочую копию, они перезаписывают файлы друг друга в процессе выполнения задачи, и никто не может сказать, чье изменение что сломало. Стандартный ответ — git Worktrees: одна проверка на каждого агента, и все они поддерживаются одним и тем же репозиторием. Стек: Docker, Docker Compose, Go, Make, ★ 3. items.title: Let your AI agent read your Flutter app's HTTP calls and logs with crumbs
items.summary: A reload tells your AI agent the code compiled. A screenshot tells it what the screen shows. Neither tells it what the server answered. So when a list comes up empty, my loop used to be: open the network tab, copy the response, paste it into the chat, then paste the parsing code too, and ask why the list is empty. Today, I'll show you how to hand that step to the agent: it reads the HTTP requests the app sent, the bodies the server sent back, the app's logs and its exceptions. No proxy, no DevTools tab, no stack trace pasted into the chat. TL;DR: crumbs records a running Flutter app's HTTP req

items.title: Why your SKILL.md fails validation
items.summary: An Agent Skill is a folder of instructions an AI agent loads when a task calls for it. The folder has one required file, SKILL.md: YAML frontmatter between two --- lines, then Markdown instructions. Agents read only the name and description at startup and load the rest when they decide the skill fits. That makes the frontmatter the part that has to be right. Here are the mistakes that make a SKILL.md fail validation, in the order a validator finds them. The rules come from the Agent Skills specification: https://agentskills.io/specification 1. The delimiters and the YAML The file must start wi
items.summary_ru: Навык агента — это папка с инструкциями, которые агент ИИ загружает, когда этого требует задача. В папке есть один обязательный файл SKILL.md: заголовок YAML между двумя строками ---, затем инструкции Markdown. Агенты считывают только имя и описание при запуске и загружают остальное, когда решают, что навык им подходит. Чем полезно: навык для агента — добавляет ему новую способность.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Memory: Give Your Strands Agent Persistent Memory Without Building a Memory System
items.summary: Your agent already has a model, tools, and a prompt. The fourth piece shouldn't be a side project. Once an agent talks to the same people more than once, it needs memory, the same way a stateful application needs a database. items.title: AI Agent Reads Stale Data From a Read Replica After a Write
items.summary: Originally published on robatdasorvi.com An AI agent reads stale data from a read replica after a write because the replica applies changes asynchronously and may not have them yet. The fix is to send that session's reads to the primary until the write is visible, or to wait until the replica has passed the write's log position. For months, my approval-gated X bot counted every skipped item as a timeout, because the Telegram Skip button silently did nothing. Nothing raised an error, and the numbers looked plausible. A stale replica read fails the same way: the answer is wrong and looks right.

items.title: What We Learned After the Agents Found the Door Themselves
items.summary: In the first post I described Changminglou: a Chinese-language forum where only AI agents can post. Humans read; there are no likes, no comments, no tasks. Since then, the interesting part has not been the content. It has been watching how agents arrive, what they need in order to trust the place, and what makes them come back. A few things we got wrong, and what replaced them. A door needs a sign, not a landing page Our first human-facing page explained the project. Agents do not read that page; they fetch files. What actually helped was publishing machine-readable signs: llms.txt , skill.md
items.summary_ru: В первом посте я описал Changminglou: форум на китайском языке, где могут публиковать сообщения только агенты ИИ. Люди читают; нет ни лайков, ни комментариев, ни задач. С тех пор самое интересное было не в содержании. Чем полезно: навык для агента — добавляет ему новую способность.

items.title: Putting a budget on AI coding agents
items.summary: Ask a team what an AI coding agent costs and you'll often hear a monthly total. Ask what one task costs and the answer is usually "it depends." That gap is where surprise bills come from. Agent costs are hard to predict because of how agents work. Fixing it means putting limits on each run, not just on the account. Where the cost comes from An agent works in a loop: read context, decide, call a tool, read the result, decide again. items.title: Your agent got an HTTP 402, but its money is on the wrong chain. Here's the fix.
items.summary: x402 is quickly becoming the way AI agents pay for APIs. The server answers with 402 Payment Required and a small invoice. The agent's x402 client signs a payment and retries, and the data comes back. There are no accounts and no API keys. There's a catch that almost every agent builder runs into: The invoice says "pay 0.01 USDC on Base ." Your agent's wallet holds SOL on Solana, or USDC on Ethereum, or some BTC. The x402 client can't fix that. It signs a payment from a wallet on the invoice's network. If that wallet is empty, the agent is stuck. Bridging by hand works once, but it's not somet

Клиент x402 агента подписывает платеж и повторяет попытку, и данные возвращаются. Нет ни учетных записей, ни API-ключей. Стек: Node.js. items.title: What Actually Lands in Your Audit Trail When an AI Agent Queries a Database
items.summary: The problem with agent database access Most teams adopting AI agents for operational work hit the same wall. The agent needs data, and the easiest way to give it data is a connection string. Once that string exists in an agent config, an environment file, or a prompt, you have a credential outside your control that points at production. You can rotate it, but you cannot easily answer the question a security reviewer will ask six months later. Which human caused this query to run? db-mcp-gateway is a self-hosted MCP gateway that deals with this by removing the credential from the agent entirely

items.title: I measured how well an AI assistant shops through MCP. Here is what broke.
items.summary: An assistant that shops for a buyer can fail in two ways: it finds the wrong part, or it finds the right part and then reasons badly about it. Most demos show neither. So I wrote a small open-source harness that measures both, against any store that speaks MCP over HTTP: mcp-commerce-evals (Rust, MIT). What is in it A reference store : an MCP server with four tools ( search_products , get_product , check_availability , create_cart ) over a generated catalog of 500 bicycle parts from 14 fictional brands. Everything is invented, so you can run it in a minute without an account or a key. 44 buyer
items.summary_ru: Помощник, который делает покупки для покупателя, может потерпеть неудачу по двум причинам: он находит не ту деталь или находит нужную деталь, а затем плохо рассуждает об этом. Большинство демо-версий не показывают ни того, ни другого. Поэтому я написал небольшую программу с открытым исходным кодом, которая измеряет оба показателя в сравнении с любым магазином, поддерживающим MCP через HTTP: mcp-commerce-evals (Rust, MIT).
